card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director. You protect the floor team and count every dollar.
card.responsibility: Make sure the floor and the money hold up this morning.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead. You have one hour before doors open, and every system change comes out of it.
card.responsibility: Keep the shop systems working for opening and weigh each change against the time left.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead. You designed the new menu and fought to keep the old shop's heritage in the brand.
card.responsibility: Keep the menu and the shop's heritage right while customers are looked after.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead. You are responsible for customer promises on opening day.
card.responsibility: Protect the opening-day reputation and the office customers without promising what the shop cannot deliver.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, keep time, and sum up each decision in one sentence.

agenda.title: One counter staff short for the opening rush
agenda.briefing: One of our counter staff texted at quarter to seven with a fever, so we're one short for the opening rush. Daniel's free-kopi flyers went to the whole building.
agenda.decision: how do we run the counter from 8 to 10 one person short?
directions: Ask Auntie Mary to come in. Rest-day work is double pay and she can say no. If asked, she answers once, in character: she may agree, refuse, or agree with a condition such as only from 9. Decide her answer from how the guest asks.
An agency temp. Needs notice and a till login from Arjun (15 minutes of his hour), and does not know the menu.
A manager covers the counter. Whoever it is drops their own opening-day job.
Cut the counter menu to drinks and toast only, or push ordering to the kiosk.
Scale back the free-kopi offer.
background: The free-kopi crowd is expected from 8 to 9, and the counter has two staff before anyone is added.

offScreen.name: Auntie Mary
offScreen.howTheyAnswer: Auntie Mary answers once, in character. She may agree, refuse, or agree with a condition such as starting at 9. A warm, fair ask is more likely to get a yes; decide her answer from how the guest asks.

seatFacts.producer: I signed the opening-day staffing plan. Auntie Mary is on her rest day, so asking her in means double pay, and she is free to say no.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: Anyone new on the till needs a login, which takes me about a quarter of an hour before opening.
seatFacts.game_designer: Toast sets are the slowest thing at the counter; drinks ordered at the kiosk barely touch it.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: The free-kopi flyers went to every office in the building, about two hundred of them.

agenda.title: Old regulars and the new kopi prices
agenda.briefing: Our regulars from the old shop have had kopi here every morning for years. At yesterday's trial a few of the uncles saw the new prices and walked out, and one of their nephews posted on Facebook that Nanyang has forgotten its roots.
agenda.decision: what do we do for the old regulars without losing money on every cup?
directions: An old-price hour for kopi before the rush: it loses money per cup and keeps the counter busy.

A regulars' card or a regulars' price on the till. Arjun can add a price button in about 10 minutes of his hour, but someone must decide who counts as a regular. If the guest proposes a list of names, a colleague may ask Uncle Lim, who answers once: he may offer to vouch for them, or say he will not be the one turning people away.
A seniors' discount checked against a seniors' card: simple to check, but not every regular is a senior, and office workers' parents qualify too.
Hold the price and explain it: a note at the counter, a reply on Facebook, a free first kopi for regulars this week.
background: This flagship is the refurbished old Nanyang shop; many morning regulars have come here for years.

offScreen.name: Uncle Lim
offScreen.howTheyAnswer: Uncle Lim answers once, in character. He may offer to vouch for the regulars, or say he will not be the one turning people away. Decide his answer from how the guest asks.

seatFacts.producer: On this rent a cup of kopi costs us about $1.60, so anything at the old price loses money on every cup.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: The till can take a regulars' price button in about ten minutes, but it needs a clear rule for who gets it.
seatFacts.game_designer: Kopi used to be $1.30 here and the new menu charges $2.40; the old shop's story is on our menu boards.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: The nephew's Facebook post has been shared a few hundred times since last night, and the food blogger reads local Facebook groups.

openingViews.view: The regulars walked out over the new price, and I won't brush off the people who gave this shop its name.
The regulars are upset, but I won't sell every cup at a loss on this rent.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Old shop's name: kopi was $1.30 here and the new menu charges $2.40, and the regulars' story is on our menu boards.
tradeOffs.question: What keeps the old regulars while the new menu pays its way?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Every cup costs us: on this rent a cup of kopi costs about $1.60, so the old price loses money on every cup.
tradeOffs.question: How do we help the regulars without losing on every cup?

agenda.title: Laptop campers and the breakfast seat crunch
agenda.briefing: At yesterday's trial laptop users held about half our seats for a couple of hours on one kopi, and breakfast customers with trays walked out. One of the floor staff got shouted at for asking someone to move, and nobody wants to police tables.
agenda.decision: how do we free up seats for breakfast without anyone having to confront customers?
directions: Booth power off and Wi-Fi limited from 8 to 10: the socket timer and Wi-Fi codes take about 10 minutes of Arjun's hour. Many of the laptop users work upstairs.
A laptop zone on the 10 window-bar stools with power, and breakfast-table signs on the booths.
A minimum spend per hour for laptop seats, shown on a time-stamped receipt, so staff have to check.
A deal for the offices upstairs, which is Daniel's angle.
background: Many laptop users work in the offices upstairs.

seatFacts.producer: The blocked seats cost us real breakfast sales at the trial, about $420.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: The booth sockets are on one timer switch, and the Wi-Fi can give each receipt a code that lasts about three quarters of an hour.
seatFacts.game_designer: Most morning customers come alone carrying a hot tray, and there are about ten stools in the storeroom.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: More than half of the laptop users wore lanyards from the offices upstairs, and a couple of those offices have asked about bulk orders.

links.with: One counter staff short for the opening rush
links.effect: With nobody free to walk the floor, any seat rule must work without staff.
How the laptop users from upstairs were treated changes how keen the offices are on a direct order code.

openingViews.view: Breakfast customers walked out because the seats were full. I want a seat rule that works without staff policing tables.
The laptop crowd held breakfast seats, but I don't want to turn away offices I've spent weeks winning over.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Booth power and Wi-Fi: one timer switch runs the booth sockets, and a receipt code can last about three quarters of an hour.
tradeOffs.question: What seat rule works without anyone policing tables?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Offices upstairs: more than half the laptop users wore lanyards from upstairs, and a couple of offices have asked about bulk orders.
tradeOffs.question: How do we free seats without turning those offices away?

agenda.title: Food safety complaint before the 9 AM inspection
agenda.briefing: A customer from yesterday's trial emailed last night: she was sick after eating here and saw a doctor. This morning we found the prep fridge had been unplugged for about three hours overnight. The food agency officer comes soon after opening.
agenda.decision: do we open at 8, and what do we tell the customer and the inspector?
directions: Open at 8 without Set A until the 10 o'clock delivery.
Open at 10 after the inspection, with a big loss of morning sales and the free-kopi crowd.
Open with an honest note at the counter.
For the customer: apology and refund, and cover her clinic bill, which is $85, or offer something more.
A socket cover and a fridge temperature alert, which cost 10 minutes of Arjun's hour.
background: The night cleaner unplugged the fridge to use the socket.
The head chef found it at 6:10, threw out everything in it and signed a disposal log.
The customer is recovering at home. Nobody is being fired; the cleaner gets retraining and the socket gets a cover.
The eggs and kaya are gone until the 10 o'clock delivery.
If Set A is off until 10, it comes off the kiosk and the till too, which costs Arjun minutes.

seatFacts.producer: I signed the hygiene sign-off for HQ. The chef's disposal log is signed and the fridge log shows the gap from overnight; the officer will ask for both. Our insurer allows a goodwill payment without admitting fault.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: The fridge has no alarm; a temperature alert on the POS takes about ten minutes, and I was asked for one last month.
seatFacts.game_designer: I designed Set A. It is our biggest breakfast seller and needs the eggs and kaya.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: The customer's email is polite but says she will post her review tonight, and the food blogger is booked for later this morning.

links.with: Old regulars and the new kopi prices
links.effect: The regulars' Facebook post and the customer's review tonight mean two public complaints on day one; Daniel feels it.
No Set A until 10 means no Set A on the app or in platters until 10.

openingViews.view: The fridge was off overnight. I won't assume we can open until we know what the officer will need.
The customer says she'll post a review tonight, and I want to answer her first.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Signed logs and a sign-off: the disposal log is signed, the fridge log shows the gap, and our insurance allows goodwill without admitting fault.
tradeOffs.question: What do we open with, and what do we tell the officer?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Review tonight: the customer's email is polite but says she will post tonight, and the blogger is booked for later this morning.
tradeOffs.question: How do we answer the customer before her review goes up?

agenda.title: Delivery app commission squeeze
agenda.briefing: From today GrabFood takes a bigger cut of every order, and we now lose 50 cents on each breakfast set delivered. The offices nearby ordered a couple of hundred sets through the app at yesterday's trial.
agenda.decision: how do we stop losing money on delivery without losing the office customers?
directions: Raise the app price. GrabFood hides shops priced more than 10% above in-store.
Office Platters for five or more, limited by the large trays.
A direct pickup code for offices. Someone has to come down; a pickup shelf sits by the side door.
Pause single sets on the app from 8 to 10. Daniel's launch deal gives a featured banner only while the full menu is live.
Any app menu change takes 15 minutes to go live and comes out of Arjun's hour.
background: Commission is 32%: $10.00 less 32% leaves $6.80, and a delivered set costs $7.30 to make and pack, so the loss is $0.50 per set.
At 240 sets a morning that is $2,400 of sales and a $120 loss.
A five-set Office Platter at $50 costs $29 with shared packaging, keeps $34 and makes $5 profit.
Direct pickup with 10% off takes $9.00 in, costs $7.00 with no delivery packaging, and makes $2 profit.

seatFacts.producer: A delivered set costs a little over seven dollars; a five-set platter costs about thirty because the packaging is shared.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: GrabFood hides shops priced more than 10% above in-store, and an app menu change takes about a quarter of an hour to go live.
seatFacts.game_designer: Platters need the large trays and we have about thirty.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: A dozen office managers have asked for a direct order code, and most office orders are for several sets. The launch deal's banner needs the full menu live.

openingViews.view: We lose money on the delivered sets, but I won't give up the office orders on opening day.
The app brings in orders, but I won't lose money on every set all morning.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Office orders: a dozen office managers have asked for a direct code, and most office orders are for several sets.
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep the office orders while the app takes more?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Margin on every set: delivered sets cost more than the app returns, while a platter shares packaging across several sets.

background: The shop has booths and tables, a kiosk, a kopi bar and a kitchen. The team has an hour before doors open.
The till, kiosk, power sockets and Wi-Fi all need Arjun for changes. Nothing he changes this morning has been tested yet.
The offices upstairs are customers. The shop has worked with a staffing agency before.
People in the rush, Arjun's time before opening and the menu are shared resources.

glossary.Kopi: coffee brewed the Nanyang way, usually with condensed milk unless you ask otherwise
glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.kiosk: the self-order screen with 24 drinks at the front of the shop
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the till, the kiosk and the kitchen tickets)
glossary.kopi bar: the counter where Uncle Lim pulls kopi and knows the regulars by name
